Emergency Water Line Repair in Sarasota, FL

Water gushing from the yard, a burst pipe or no water at all? Shut off the main valve first. Then call SRQ Leak Pros to reach a local pro for emergency water line repair.

Call (941) 541-0938
  • Sarasota & Manatee counties
  • Service lines, slabs, sewers & pools
  • Homes, condos & businesses
  • Independent local providers

Quick answer: Emergency water line repair in Sarasota starts with you: close the main shut-off valve to stop the flow. If water is pouring from the meter box or the street, report it to your utility. Then a local pro can find the break, make a fast repair and test the line.

A burst water line can move a lot of water fast. Inside, it soaks floors, walls and cabinets. Outside, it can wash out the sand under a driveway or flood a flower bed. The first ten minutes matter most, and most of what you need to do in those minutes is free.

First steps in a water line emergency

  1. Close the main shut-off valve. It is usually where the water line enters the house, often on an outside wall, in the garage or near the water heater. Turn a lever handle a quarter turn so it sits across the pipe.
  2. If you can't find it, close the valve at the meter. Many meter boxes have a customer-side valve. Some need a meter key.
  3. Turn off the water heater. Switch off power or set a gas heater to pilot so it doesn't run empty.
  4. Keep away from wet outlets. If water reaches electrical outlets or panels, stay clear and shut off power only if it is safe to reach the breaker.
  5. Take photos. Pictures of the break and any damage help with insurance.
  6. Call for help. Report breaks on the utility's side to the utility. For your side, call to reach a local pro.

Your side or the utility's side?

Where the water is coming from tells you who to call first.

What you seeLikely ownerWho to call first
Water bubbling in the street or a hydrantUtilityYour water utility
Water rising inside the meter boxOften the utilityYour water utility
Water gushing in the yard between meter and houseOwnerA local water line pro
Burst pipe inside walls, attic or garageOwnerA local pro, after shutting the main
No water at all, neighbors have waterOften ownerCheck the main valve, then a local pro
No water at all, neighbors also outUtilityYour water utility

City of Sarasota Utilities asks residents to report leaks in the street, at manholes, hydrants, meter boxes or backflow devices. Sarasota County's leak FAQ says customers without water are a high priority for its crews. Leaks on private property are the owner's to fix.

What emergency water line repair includes

  • Confirming the main is closed and the flow has stopped
  • Finding the break by sight, sound or a quick pressure test
  • A temporary or permanent repair, depending on the pipe
  • Locate marks or an 811 ticket before any digging
  • A pressure test after the repair
  • Restoring water and checking for other leaks
  • A written note on the pipe's condition and any follow-up work

Common water line emergencies

  • Broken yard line. Often caused by digging, a fence post, a root or a failing old pipe.
  • Burst pipe in the attic or wall. Old fittings, high pressure or a failed connector can let go suddenly.
  • Polybutylene failure. Gray plastic pipe from about 1978 to 1997 can split at fittings without warning.
  • Water heater supply line failure. A flexible connector bursts and floods the garage or closet.
  • Line damaged during work. A contractor or homeowner strikes a pipe while digging.

How a fast repair works

  1. Stop the water. The main is closed if it isn't already.
  2. Find the break. Visible breaks are opened up; hidden ones are found with a pressure test and listening tools.
  3. Make it safe. A repair coupling, clamp or new section restores the pipe.
  4. Test. Water is turned back on slowly and the line is checked under pressure.
  5. Plan next steps. If the pipe is failing along its length, you'll get a quote for a full water line replacement.

What affects the cost

Prices depend on what broke and where. Emergency work done after normal business hours may cost more. Ask about this on the call.

  • Location of the break: yard, slab, wall or attic
  • Pipe material and size
  • Whether digging and 811 locates are needed
  • After-hours or weekend timing
  • Water damage cleanup, which is a separate job

DIY vs. calling a pro

Closing the main is the most useful thing you can do. A quick clamp from a hardware store may slow a small leak on an exposed pipe until help arrives. Don't dig in the yard to find a broken line, because gas, power and communication lines may be buried nearby. Florida requires a call to Sunshine 811 before digging.

Insurance and Florida notes

Many homeowners policies cover sudden water damage from a burst pipe, but not the worn-out pipe itself or long-term leaks. Take photos and keep receipts. Florida Statutes § 627.70132 requires notice of a property insurance claim within 1 year after the date of loss. Talk with your agent about your policy. This is general information, not legal advice.

Repairs to water lines fall under Florida's plumbing contractor rules. Ask the provider for a license number.

Local note

Local note: barrier-island homes on Siesta Key and Longboat Key are often empty for part of the year, so a burst line can run for days. Find your main shut-off now. In North Port, long service lines mean a yard break may be far from the house.

Emergency Water Line Repair questions

What should I do first when a water line bursts?

Close the main shut-off valve to stop the water. Then turn off the water heater, keep away from wet electrical outlets, and call for help.

Where is the main water shut-off in a Florida home?

It is often on an outside wall where the line enters the house, in the garage, or near the water heater. Some homes rely on a valve at the meter box.

Who do I call if water is coming up in the street?

Call your water utility. Breaks in the street, at hydrants or inside the meter box are usually the utility's to fix.

Will insurance cover a burst pipe?

Many policies cover sudden water damage, but often not the pipe itself or slow leaks. Check your policy and talk with your agent.

Can I use water after a temporary repair?

Usually, once the pro has tested the line. Ask whether the repair is temporary or permanent and when follow-up work is needed.
